Subject: Spike in 429/5xx after org limit change — urgent

Hi Hannah —

We started seeing a large number of 429s and a few 504 timeouts hitting our ingestion route around 08:45 PST after we completed the org->project quota cutover you recommended. Traffic is steady but error rate jumped to ~18% for ~30 minutes. Attached is a short log extract and a dashboard screenshot.

This is affecting our nightly batch jobs and the customer-facing verification UI. Can you confirm whether any rate-limiter or tiering mapping changed on your side? We rolled forward at 08:30 and immediately began seeing retries from our workers that made it worse.

From our end we paused retries and backed off; errors subsided when we throttled job concurrency. We need a timeline of root cause and an ETA for a fix — senior leadership is asking.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in 429/5xx after org limit change — urgent

Hannah — quick status:
- We have a 429 flood recorded on front-door for api.medverify with spike starting 08:41 PST, peak 08:50 PST. The source is a sudden drop in effective quota tokens due to the cutover job that applied a project-level cap one tier lower than the org default.
- The quota migration script had a mapping file with an off-by-one tier index for 2 projects (MV-prod and MV-batch). That caused their burst allowance to collapse under expected traffic.
- When clients retried aggressively the rate-limiter entered token exhaustion faster and transient 5xxs followed due to queue pressure downstream.

Mitigation applied 09:15 PST: rolled back the mapping for MV-prod and increased temporary burst allowance. We also enabled a short-lived soft-fail path to route non-critical requests to a lower-cost model variant to shed load. Errors dropped to ~0.8% by 09:28 PST.

Next steps:
1) Patch the migration script to validate mapping ranges and add a dry-run check (INF-7421).
2) Add telemetry alert for sudden quota token drops per-org so we can auto-roll forward temporary allowances.
3) Propose a credit for impacted window and a postmortem with MedVerify.

I will attach the gateway traces and a short mitigation playbook.

Marcus
Staff Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in 429/5xx after org limit change — urgent

Priya — thank you for the quick heads up and for the logs. Short summary from our side: a migration mapping error reduced MV's effective burst quota for two projects which, combined with aggressive retries, caused a transient surge in 429s and some downstream 504s. Marcus has rolled back the mapping and applied a temporary burst uplift; we put a soft-fail routing in place to protect the critical verification path.

What you can expect from us:
- Incident report and timeline (by EOD Wed) — includes root cause and the migration patch.
- INF-7421: change to prevent off-by-one mapping and add dry-run validation.
- A one-time service credit for the impacted window (Mar 1 08:40–09:30 PST). Marissa will follow up with a formal credit note and exec comms.
- Short-term alerting change so a quota token drop >10% within 5m triggers auto-rollback.

Priya, can you confirm the exact customer-facing windows to include in the invoice/credit? Also, please send any downstream error samples if you have more than the attached log.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is sensitive for your nightly jobs. We'll share the postmortem when complete and set up a short readout with your ops and engineering leads if helpful.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
